questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: The demand curve each firm faces
questions.learningObjective: Identify why a monopolist faces downward-sloping demand
questions.stem: An amateur astronomer logs that a single telescope maker must cut price to sell more; what follows for demand?

options.text: The firm faces a downward-sloping demand curve
The firm faces a horizontal demand curve at market price
The firm faces a vertical demand curve at any price
The firm faces an upward-sloping demand curve

questions.explanation: A monopolist is the market, so selling more requires lowering price. The horizontal curve describes perfect competition.

questions.topic: Why marginal revenue sits below price
questions.learningObjective: Explain why marginal revenue is below price
questions.stem: A star-chart seller notes she must lower price on all charts to sell an extra one; why is MR below price?

options.text: Because fixed costs rise with each extra unit
Because the price cut applies only to the extra unit
options.misconception: ignores revenue lost on previous units

options.text: Because the price cut applies to all units sold
Because demand becomes perfectly elastic at high output

questions.explanation: Lowering price reduces revenue on units already sold, so MR falls below price. The wrong idea assumes only the new unit gets the lower price.
questions.hint: Think about revenue on prior units.
